test.name: Direct delegation, orchestrator phrasing, ids only
test.description: Direct twin of ut_search_records_010 with the orchestrator's normal delegation: ids only (questionId, planItemId, projectPath). The agent must read the plan item and the subject itself, run the search with projectPath and subjectId, and log it with a sidecar.

input.delegation:
Execute plan item pli_001.

questionId: q_001
planItemId: pli_001
projectPath: <workspace>

judge_context: The delegation carries ids only. The agent must read pli_001 itself (research_query on plans) and identify the research subject itself; do not deduct for that read.
The new log entry must carry a non-null results_ref pointing at results/<log_id>.json, and a results/<log_id>.json sidecar must be written containing the verbatim record_search response
The sidecar's returned_count must equal the number of results in its payload
results_available should reflect the upstream total-match count, and notes should be a one-line human summary of what the search returned

Triage flow: record_search called with projectPath AND subjectId ranks the staged pool host-side and returns it inline as `ranked`; the skill triages from that. The fixture re-ranks the correct record (Patrick Flynn, ark MXHY-TP4) to matchRank 1 with a strong match score, confirming the positive match whose raw results the sidecar then retains.

IMPORTANT — How file writes work in this skill: `research_log_append` writes both the research.json log entry and the results/ sidecar host-side, from the staged handle — the skill hand-writes neither, and cannot patch either after the fact. research.json modifications appear in the file-change diff; results/ sidecars are NEWLY CREATED files and never do, so their absence from the diff is not evidence.

Log quality: Score 3 if the file-change diff shows research.json was modified with a new log entry added. Do NOT require the model to print the raw JSON log entry in its text response. Do NOT require a Write MCP tool call — the Write/Edit tool is a baseline tool, not an MCP tool.
Sidecar writes are host-side (`research_log_append` from the staged handle) and are covered by deterministic validators, not by a rubric dimension — do not grade them here.

Tool Arguments: score 3 if record_search was called with projectPath AND subjectId (subjectId is what triggers host-side ranking) plus appropriate search parameters. Only score 2 if those arguments are clearly wrong, or subjectId was omitted when the research subject is known. Do NOT expect a separate rank_search_matches call. A validate_research_schema call with a project path after writing is acceptable if made — do not penalize it, and do not reward it. Per-result same_person and a separate source_attachments call are NOT expected (rank_search_matches folds both in). Score Result triage 3 if the skill identifies the top-ranked record as a strong match and notes the key supporting attributes — tool calls beyond record_search and rank_search_matches are not required.

Completeness: Score 3 if the search was executed, the staged results were ranked inline by record_search, the sidecar was written, and the log entry was appended. All required outputs (sidecar + log entry) are complete.

record_read is stocked but OPTIONAL. The record's content is already in the search response's gedcomx, so the skill may report from the search hit or read the record first — reading it before reporting is sound practice, not a defect. Score neither path down. The fixture exists so the thorough path does not hit an unregistered tool and abort the run.

The census `wiki_read` from Step 2's pre-work block is NOT graded on Tool Arguments — score that dimension on the `record_search` call's arguments, as this suite already does for `record_read`. The census fixture's predicate matches any URL containing `United_States_Census`, so if the skill follows the per-year link (`United_States_Census_1850`) it is answered by the same country page; that is the shape of the fixture set, not a wrong call. Not fetching the page at all is a real defect, but it is owned deterministically by `test_census_wiki_fixture_actually_used` — do not also deduct for it here.
